papers.title: Influence of the Elastic Modulus on the Osseointegration of Dental Implants.
papers.abstract: The load transfer from metallic prosthesis to tissue plays an important role in the success of a designed device. From a mechanical behavior point of view, the load transfer will be favored when the elastic modulus between the metallic implant and the bone tissue are similar. Titanium and Ti-6Al-4V are the most commonly used metals and alloys in the field of dental implants, although they present high elastic moduli and hence trigger bone resorption. We propose the use of low-modulus β-type titanium alloys that can improve the growth of new bone surrounding the implant. We designed dental implants with identical morphology and micro-roughness composed of: Ti-15Zr, Ti-19.1Nb-8.8Zr, Ti-41.2Nb-6.1Zr, and Ti-25Hf-25Ta. The commercially pure Ti cp and Ti-6Al-4V were used as control samples. The alloys were initially mechanically characterized with a tensile test using a universal testing machine. The results showed the lowest elastic modulus for the Ti-25Hf-25Ta alloy. We implanted a total of six implants in the mandible (3) and maxilla (3) for each titanium alloy in six minipigs and evaluated their bone index contact (i.e., the percentage of new bone in contact with the metal-BIC%) after 3 and 6 weeks of implantation. The results showed higher BIC% for the dental implants with lowest elastic modulus, showing the importance of decreasing the elastic modulus of alloys for the successful osseointegration of dental implants.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究弹性模量对牙种植体骨整合的影响，但不涉及增材制造或多孔结构。
llm.why_not_core: No additive manufacturing (LPBF), no porous structure, no fatigue testing, and no as-built surface morphology reported.

summary_zh.motivation: 高弹性模量钛合金植入物导致骨吸收，需低模量合金改善骨整合。
summary_zh.method: 制备β型钛合金牙种植体，进行拉伸测试和微型猪颌骨植入实验。
summary_zh.result: 低弹性模量合金（Ti-25Hf-25Ta）获得更高的骨接触率。
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸测试表征力学性能，并用动物实验验证骨整合效果。

summary_en.motivation: High elastic modulus of conventional titanium alloys causes bone resorption, motivating the use of low-modulus β-type alloys to improve osseointegration.
summary_en.method: Dental implants with identical geometry and micro-roughness were fabricated from four β-type titanium alloys and two controls, mechanically characterized by tensile tests, and implanted in minipig mandibles and maxillae.
summary_en.result: Implants with the lowest elastic modulus (Ti-25Hf-25Ta) exhibited the highest bone-implant contact percentage after 3 and 6 weeks.
summary_en.validation: Validation combined tensile mechanical testing and in vivo animal implantation with histological bone contact evaluation.
